title: Event envelope gating and client capability negotiation for analytics rollout
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: This ticket implements a backwards-compatible rollout mechanism for analytics event envelopes across SDK/CLI/API clients and the ingestion pipeline. Rather than a hard-cut schema bump, we'll add a capability negotiation header + event 'envelope_version' field and gate new fields behind per-client feature flags and server-side capability checks. The goals are: (1) ensure no client-side crashes when new optional fields appear, (2) give visibility into adoption by client version, and (3) enable incremental rolling transforms in the analytics pipeline with an easy rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDKs/CLI emit events with an optional 'envelope_version' and 'capabilities' header when available; 2) Ingestion accepts both v1 and v2 envelopes for at least 4 weeks; 3) Console dashboards show percent of traffic by envelope_version and per-sdk-version adoption; 4) Dual-write (shadow) path implemented so transformed v2 events are validated without affecting production flows; 5) Rollback can be triggered via runtime feature flag to stop honoring v2 fields and revert to v1 extraction path.
implementation_notes: High-level plan: 1) Define minimal capability negotiation wire-format (HTTP header 'X-RW-Client-Capabilities': csv of tokens; body field 'envelope_version'). 2) SDK/CLI: add opt-in flag --telemetry-envelope=v2 and emit header with semantic capability tokens (e.g., 'kv-cache-v1,structured-output-hints'). 3) Gateway/API: accept header and annotate incoming request metadata; route to ingestion with 'source_envelope' tag. 4) Ingestion pipeline: add transform stage that checks 'source_envelope' and either runs v1 extractors or v2 extractors; when in shadow mode, run both and log diffs to a validation topic. 5) Observability: add dashboard on Kibana/Datadog for envelope_version, client capability tokens, transform error rates, and percent of events failing v2-only parsers. 6) Rollout: start with internal SDKs only -> small customer cohort -> gradual ramp controlled by console feature flag + server-side sampling. 7) Backwards compatibility: unknown capabilities are ignored; v2 fields must be optional with clear fallback semantics.
tradeoffs:
- Strongly typed v2 fields enable richer analytics but increase risk of fragile clients; hence opt-in and feature-flagged approach.
- Dual-write/shadow increases pipeline cost and complexity, but is necessary for confidence before flipping the switch.
- Doing schema migration purely server-side (no client opt-in) would be faster but risks client breakage and provides less visibility per-client.
risks:
- Clients that keep older SDKs will not send capability tokens; must preserve v1 extraction permanently for those customers or provide automated client update prompts.
- Shadow validation may show many diffs initially; we need triage runbooks to classify diffs (benign vs data-loss).
- Security: new richer fields may include PII; must run through privacy review and ensure PII filtering/encryption.
- Latency: additional checks in Gateway add ~1-3ms; benchmark in staging.
migration_strategy: Phase A (internal): enable v2 opt-in for internal SDKs + CI job that sends test corpus -> validation topic. Phase B (beta customers): invite small set via console toggle; dual-write true -> run v2 pipeline in shadow and monitor diffs for 2 weeks. Phase C (gradual ramp): increase beta by sample rates and add more SDK releases with v2 enabled by default. Phase D (flip): when metrics stable (error <0.05% and adoption >75% across active SDKs), change ingestion default to prefer v2 extraction and deprecate v1 after 90 days.
tasks: Design review and signatures (privacy, security, product)
SDK changes: add header + opt-in flag, update docs
Gateway changes: header parsing + routing tags
Ingestion transforms: implement v2 extractor + shadow mode
Observability: dashboards, alerts, validation topic consumers
QA: end-to-end tests, fuzz corpus, performance bench
Runbook: rollback steps and escalation paths
